hypotheses.reasoning: The origin is the third-party translation API called by catalog-svc. Its latency climbed from a normal state to 4.8s at #168 (20:43:23), then 12s at #171, then calls began failing with 30s upstream timeouts (#181, #184, #199). Those hung calls tie up catalog-svc, which makes search-api's GET /products/batch calls time out (#182, #185, #200). search-api's connection pool to catalog-svc then saturates (#198, #210) and checkouts time out (#221). That exhausted pool is what turns into web-bff 503s (#201, #205, #213, #223, #227, #229, #240). catalog-db, redis-cache and index-worker logged no errors and look healthy, so they are not the cause. The bff 503s and pool saturation are downstream symptoms and I have not cited them as the fault. The hang-not-fail-fast pattern points to dependency_timeout rather than external_outage.
If the translation vendor is down or degraded on its side, the same lines would fit an external outage. The evidence favours a hang over a fast-fail 5xx, so this is the less likely reading.

verdict.recommendedAction: Engage the translation API provider and check its status. In catalog-svc, add a hard client timeout and circuit breaker around the translate call (well under 30s) so it cannot hold connections, and serve untranslated or cached results as a fallback. Bound the search-api to catalog-svc pool and add fast-fail on getBatch so the 503 cascade stops. Once translate calls recover, verify the search error rate returns to baseline.
